answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on trades or earn reputation. If several identities endorse a fraudulent deal and evidence proves collusion, the protocol confiscates their deposits and removes their endorsements; splitting one actor into many names therefore multiplies the capital at risk, rather than multiplying influence for free. The ferrous ledger might track stake, while sable and orchard label markets, not identities. This deters Sybils, though it cannot stop wealthy attackers or guarantee honest judgments.
